nodes.name: Electrochemical transformation to corrugated β-Ni(OH)₂
nodes.procedure: The corrugated β-Ni(OH)₂ was obtained after 9th CV cycling within voltage window of 0-0.7 V using 6 M KOH electrolyte. The CV measurement was conducted on Bio-Logic SP-200 workstation with three-electrode setup (Hg/HgO reference, Pt foil counter), using NiV-LDH/CFP as working electrode. Electrochemical reaction: 4 Ni₀.₇₅V₀.₂₅(CO₃²⁻)₀.₁₂₅(OH⁻)₂·H₂O + 2 OH⁻ → 3 Ni(OH)₂ + VO₂ + 6 H₂O + 0.5 CO₃²⁻ + e⁻.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiV-LDH shows vertically oriented nanosheets with lateral size ≈600-800 nm on CFP; after 5th and 9th CV cycles (0.7-5, 0.7-9), develops slightly curved then highly curved morphology.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The scanning electron microscopy (SEM) images show that vertically oriented NiV-LDH nanosheets with a lateral size of ≈600 to 800 nm self-assemble on the CFP (Figure 1b and Figure S1a,b, Supporting Information)... After the 5th cyclic voltammetry (CV) cycle over a voltage window of 0-0.7 V, the nanosheets (denoted as 0.7-5) show a slightly curved structure... After the 9th CV cycling (0-0.7 V), the nanosheets (denoted as 0.7-9) develop a highly curved morphology.

properties.description: Scanning Electron Microscopy image showing nanostructured material with ruffled, sheet-like morphology

nodes.characterization_summary: NiV-LDH shows lattice fringes ≈0.20 nm (018) and 0.26 nm (012) planes; after 5th cycle shows disorder phase and dislocations; after 9th cycle shows crystalline grains with disordered domains and 0.27 nm (100) β-Ni(OH)₂ spacing.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HR-TEM) image of NiV-LDH shows the visible lattice fringes with a spacing of ≈0.20 nm and 0.26 nm (Figure 1c), which can be assigned to the (018) and (012) planes of LDH phase, respectively... accompanied by the formation of disorder phase and dislocations (Figure 1d,e)... the lattice spacing of 0.27 nm corresponds to the (100) planes of β-Ni(OH)₂.

nodes.characterization_summary: After 9th CV cycling, corrugated β-Ni(OH)₂ shows small crystalline grains surrounded by disordered domains with lattice spacing of 0.27 nm corresponding to (100) planes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The HR-TEM image (Figure 1g) shows that the small crystalline grains are surrounded by interspersed disordered domains, and the lattice spacing of 0.27 nm corresponds to the (100) planes of β-Ni(OH)₂.

nodes.characterization_summary: Vanadium atomic concentration in NiV-LDH decreases from 22.2% to 1.6% after 5th cycle and to 0 after 9th cycle.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The energy-dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) result reveals that the atomic concentration of vanadium in NiV-LDH rapidly decreases from 22.2% to 1.6% after the 5th cycle, and then further drops to 0 after the 9th cycle (Figure S2, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: No α-Ni(OH)₂ peaks after 5th cycle; new peaks indexed to β-Ni(OH)₂ (001), (100), (101), (110) planes; c-axis spacing 7.8→4.6 Å, a/b-axis expansion 3.08→3.12 Å (1.3% tensile strain); corrugated β-Ni(OH)₂ shows reduced crystallinity vs regular β-Ni(OH)₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns further reveal a phase transformation from the α-Ni(OH)₂ to the β-Ni(OH)₂ that occurs during the CV cycling (Figure S4, Supporting Information). Specifically, no diffraction peaks of α-Ni(OH)₂ are detected after the 5th cycle... Such a phase transformation not only leads to a dramatic decrease in interlayer spacing along c-axis (from 7.8 to 4.6 Å), but also results in a 1.3% tensile strain along a and b-axis due to the expansion of the lattice parameter from 3.08 to 3.12 Å (Figure 1a).

nodes.characterization_summary: Operando Ni K-edge FT-EXAFS shows peaks at 1.59 and 2.75 Å intensity gradually reduces upon cycling; positive shift of Ni-Ni/V peaks indicates increased bond length.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Fourier transform (FT) of the extended XAFS (FT-EXAFS) spectra reveal that the intensity of the two peaks at 1.59 and 2.75 Å gradually reduces upon cycling (Figure 1h), indicating that more Ni cations transform into a state with unsaturated coordination. The positive shift of Ni-Ni/V peaks further implies an increment in the Ni-Ni/V bond length upon CV cycling.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni-O coordination number decreases from 6.0 to 5.4 then 5.0; Ni-Ni/V coordination number from 6.0 to 5.1 then 4.5; Ni-Ni/V bond length increases from 3.08 to 3.12 then 3.15 Å indicating tensile strain of 1.3% and 2.3%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 1i and the EXAFS fitting results (Figure S5 and Table S1, Supporting Information), after the 5th and the 9th cycles, the Ni-O coordination number (N(Ni-O)) is decreased from 6.0 to 5.4, and then to 5.0... the Ni-Ni/V bond length is increased from 3.08 to 3.12, and then to 3.15 Å after the 5th and the 9th cycles, indicative of an increased tensile strain of 1.3% and 2.3% along the a- and b-axis.

nodes.characterization_summary: Operando V K-edge XANES shows monotonic oxidation of V during 1st CV cycle shifting toward high energy.
nodes.evidence_snippet: It is clearly seen that the V K-edge XANES spectrum shifts toward high energy (Figure 2b), which implies the monotonic oxidation of V during the 1st cycle.

nodes.characterization_summary: V L-edge and O K-edge spectra show decreasing intensity of V L₃ and L₂-edge peaks after 5th cycle and complete disappearance after 9th cycle due to vanadium dissolution.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in the V L-edge and O K-edge spectra... the intensity of both V L₃-edge and L₂-edge decreases after the 5th cycle and completely disappears after the 9th cycle.

nodes.characterization_summary: O K-edge RIXS maps show suppression of features at 533.7 and 536.0 eV (O 2p to V 3d) after 9th cycle indicating V-O bond breaking in bulk.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in the O K-edge RIXS maps (Figure 2e), the two features centered at excitation energy of 533.7 and 536.0 eV (assigned to the O 2p to V 3d hybrid state) exist in the pristine NiV-LDH. After the 9th cycle, these two features are completely suppressed in the RIXS map.

nodes.characterization_summary: WT-EXAFS over Ni K-edge shows gradually disappearing intensity maximum at ≈7 Å⁻¹ (Ni-V coordination) indicating Ni-V bond breaking.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 2g, the gradually disappearing intensity maximum at ≈7 Å⁻¹ (assigned to the Ni-V coordination) also indicates the Ni-V bond breaking in the bulk of the electrode.

nodes.characterization_summary: Regular and corrugated β-Ni(OH)₂ show same β-Ni(OH)₂ phase but corrugated shows reduced crystallinity and (100) peak shift to lower angle indicating larger lattice constant.
nodes.evidence_snippet: XRD patterns further show that both regular and corrugated β-Ni(OH)₂ nanosheets have the same β-Ni(OH)₂ phase [JCPDS Card no. 14-0017]. While the regular β-Ni(OH)₂ is highly crystalline, the corrugated β-Ni(OH)₂ shows reduced crystallinity (Figure S11, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: Regular β-Ni(OH)₂ and α-Ni(OH)₂ show saturated coordination environment of Ni sites contrasting vacancy-enriched structure of corrugated β-Ni(OH)₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The EXAFS curve-fitting analysis further reveals the saturated coordination environment of Ni sites in both regular β-Ni(OH)₂ and α-Ni(OH)₂ (Figure S12 and Table S2, Supporting Information), which contrasts the vacancy-enriched lattice structure of the corrugated β-Ni(OH)₂.

nodes.characterization_summary: Reduced semicircle diameter in EIS reveals improved charge carrier transport properties in corrugated β-Ni(OH)₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The reduced semicircle diameter shown in electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) further reveals the improved transport properties of the charge carriers in the corrugated β-Ni(OH)₂ (Figure S15, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: Regular β-Ni(OH)₂ monocrystalline and α-Ni(OH)₂ polycrystalline confirmed by HR-TEM and FFT patterns.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The HR-TEM image and fast Fourier transform (FFT) patterns further confirm the monocrystalline and polycrystalline structure of regular β-Ni(OH)₂ and α-Ni(OH)₂, respectively.
